summary: The appeal challenges the Gujarat High Court's order granting bail to respondent no.2, the accused in a murder case. The prosecution alleged that the accused conspired to kill his wife for monetary gains through insurance, using a hired driver to hit her with a car, initially reported as an accident. Investigation revealed call records linking the accused and co-accused prior to the incident, supporting a criminal conspiracy under Sections 302, 120(B), and 114 IPC. The High Court granted bail, citing circumstantial evidence and the accused's societal roots. The Supreme Court examined whether this decision ignored the gravity of the offense, the strength of material evidence, and settled bail principles.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 21 of the Constitution of India
Ramesh Bhavan Rathod v. Vishanbhai Hirabhai Makwana (Koli), (2021) 6 SCC 630
Bhoopendra Singh v. State of Rajasthan & another
Gudikanti Narasimhulu & Ors. v. Public Prosecutor, (1978) 1 SCC 240
Prahlad Singh Bhati v. NCT of Delhi & ORS, (2001) 4 SCC 280
final_judgment: The appeal is allowed. The impugned order of the High Court granting bail to respondent no.2 is set aside. The respondent no.2 shall surrender to custody forthwith and the trial court may consider any future bail application on its merits.
